idea: delete each word and re-score; a word whose removal raises the predicted grade is dead weight

training_data.sources: Humicroedit task-1 train + task-2 train (both edits per row)

controlled_pair_validation.note: restricted to pairs whose BOTH members are in the held-out split, so this is out-of-sample; an earlier version scored all pairs including trained rows and reported 0.75, which measured memorisation as much as preference

demo.setup: I told my therapist about my fear of speed bumps.
demo.punchline: She said I am actually just slowly getting over it honestly.

honesty: the deletion profile is only as good as the model; held-out spearman is reported above and is small, so treat per-word deltas as a ranked suggestion rather than a verdict

known_failure_mode.what: On the demo joke the tool ranks 'getting' and 'slowly' as dead weight. Those two words ARE the pun: 'slowly getting over it' is the whole reframe. Cutting them destroys the joke.
known_failure_mode.why: Every feature this model sees is structural - lengths, syllables, rarity, punctuation, position. None of them encode meaning, so the model cannot know that a common, unremarkable word is carrying the reframe. It sees two ordinary words adding length to a punchline, and length is the strongest thing it has learned.
known_failure_mode.what_the_tool_is_actually_good_for: structural dead weight: hedges, trailing adverbs, filler like 'honestly' and 'just', which it does rank at the top. It is a filler detector, not a pun detector, and should be described that way.
known_failure_mode.the_fix_not_yet_built: add semantic features that tie a punchline word back to the setup - embedding similarity to the setup, or the per-token surprisal drop the certified instrument already measures. A word whose removal collapses the setup-punchline link is load-bearing however common it looks.
known_failure_mode.why_this_is_stated_rather_than_tuned_awa: the demo could have been chosen to hide this. A tool that advises comedians has to publish the case where it gives bad advice.

headline_result.context: the pinned single-signal Humicroedit validation reached spearman 0.115; a 30-feature gradient-boosted model on 28,414 graded rows reaches 0.5075 on 8,525 held-out rows, and picks the human-preferred edit in a controlled pair 0.707 of the time out of sample
